source.contamination_note: public, widely-referenced repo (6k+ stars, grounds several real tools in our own corpus — see evals/golden/detection/README.md) — treat any recall measured against it as [contamination-risk], not proof of novel-detection capability. source.note: 909 .sol fixtures total as of this commit (far more than the ~550-681 cited in earlier research rounds — the repo keeps growing monthly, e.g. src/test/2026-08/). This manifest catalogs 8, not a forced 10 — dropped 2 candidates (ValueDefi/Cover) after checking their source: only a bare testExploit()/test() function and fork block were confirmable, no independently verifiable root-cause detail, so excluded rather than guessed at.

cases.description: Euler Finance: flash loan 30M DAI -> deposit+leverage via mint() -> donateToReserves() deliberately worsens own health factor below liquidation threshold -> attacker's own second account liquidates the now-undercollateralized position at a discount for a large eDAI/dDAI mismatch. Root cause per file: donateToReserves() had no check against self-inflicted insolvency.
cases.source_richness: high — file has @Analysis/@TX headers with tweet + Etherscan tx links and a 10-step summary

cases.description: Nomad Bridge: a Replica contract's trusted root was mistakenly initialized to 0x00 (a value that trivially "proves" any message), so ANY calldata could be replayed/crafted to withdraw funds — became a free-for-all copy-paste exploit once discovered. ~$152M lost per the file's own @KeyInfo header.
cases.source_richness: high — @KeyInfo header cites total loss, proxy/logic addresses, and the Nomad audit report finding (QSP-19) that had flagged this exact issue

cases.description: bZx (original, one of the earliest famous flash-loan oracle-manipulation attacks) — file cites attacker/vulnerable-contract/attack-tx Etherscan links directly.
cases.source_richness: medium — addresses and tx cited, no step-by-step summary in this particular file

cases.description: A later, separate bZx-related incident (~$208K per file) — file cites two BlockSec-explorer attack-tx links and a postmortem thread; mechanism not independently re-derived from the contract body for this catalog entry.
cases.source_richness: medium — loss amount and tx links confirmed, root-cause mechanism [NOT_COVERED] in this pass

cases.description: Harvest Finance: setup wires a Curve y-pool and Uniswap V2 ETH/USDC+ETH/USDT LPs alongside Harvest's own USDC pool — confirms the well-known flash-loan Curve-pool price manipulation shape, though the exact step sequence wasn't re-derived line-by-line for this catalog entry.
cases.source_richness: medium — confirmed via constructor/state wiring, not a written summary in the file itself

cases.description: Inverse Finance: wires multiple Curve/Vyper pool contracts (curve3pool, yvCurve3Crypto, curveRegistry) and forks mainnet at a specific historical block (14,972,418) — confirms a Curve-pool-pricing-based exploit shape.
cases.source_richness: medium — auto-generated file (abi-to-sol), confirmed via wiring + fork block, no written summary

cases.description: Rari Capital: `testExploit()` takes a `vault.flashLoan(...)` and implements `receiveFlashLoan(...)` — confirms a flash-loan-borrowed callback shape, consistent with the publicly documented Fuse pools cross-contract reentrancy incident, though the reentrant call path wasn't re-traced line-by-line for this entry.
cases.source_richness: medium — auto-generated file, confirmed via flashLoan/receiveFlashLoan function presence

cases.description: Qubit Finance (QBridge): file declares two overloaded `deposit(...)` interface signatures on the bridge contract — consistent with the publicly documented missing-validation-on-a-legacy-deposit-overload root cause, though not independently re-derived from the exploit body for this entry.
cases.source_richness: medium — confirmed via interface declarations, no written summary in the file
